A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HedgeSpec research work. Their full text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama/Qwen inference experiments, acceptance and throughput measurements, overhead analysis, ablations, and routing experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds Bird/MultiNews, SpecBench, and REST/Vicuna experiments in Tables 12–14.

M1.justification: The counterfactual estimator, NormalHedge selection, delayed feedback, and hybrid/skipped updates are retained. The REST experiment instantiates the existing framework; new Figure 7 documents the already-used NormalHedge algorithm without introducing a different selection rule.

E1.justification: v2 retains existing coverage and adds Bird, MultiNews, SpecBench, MT-Bench, and Alpaca evaluations. SpecBench explicitly includes Natural Questions, translation, and RAG-style workloads without matching specialist drafters, substantially broadening the demonstrated task coverage.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain their comparator membership. The added studies reuse UCBSpec, EXP3Spec, and autoregressive references. REST is an additional decoding framework, while Medusa and PLD are discussed without new comparative measurements.

E3.justification: Existing EAGLE settings remain unchanged, but v2 adds distinct evaluation configurations: SpecBench uses seven specialists plus an EAGLE generalist, and REST uses Vicuna-7B-v1.5 with seven domain-specific retrieval drafters. These are additional experimental designs, not revisions to the original runs.

E4.justification: Appendix D.8 adds a robustness check where SpecBench requests lack matching specialists and the pool includes a generalist fallback. It does not isolate the fallback's effect through an ablation. Existing loss/learner ablations, pool-size analyses, and prompt-shift routing tests are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new estimator-variance argument is theoretical rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 and the original GSM8K/HumanEval entries remain unchanged. Added benchmark and REST results substantially extend the evidence: REST HumanEval reports 55.27 tokens/s for HedgeSpec versus 44.60 for UCBSpec. The new Llama MultiNews result also reveals an exception: HedgeSpec's 65.20 tokens/s trails EAGLE's 66.10.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the conditional estimator-variance bound K²/4 using Popoviciu's inequality and contrasts it with EXP3Spec. Appendix B.3 removes the short Hedge-reduction proof of Theorem 6 while retaining its statement. The central theorems and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim full-information drafter selection without additional target calls, no-regret guarantees, improved dependence on drafter count over bandits, broad decoding compatibility, and practical speedups. The shortened conclusion and additional experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New discussion explains why missing specialists motivate a generalist in SpecBench. Appendix D.9 adds applicability conditions and distinguishes PLD's single-drafter limitation, potential Medusa integration, and demonstrated REST integration. Earlier censoring and joint-training interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project code link, explicit NormalHedge initialization and update pseudocode, and REST target/pool specifications. Appendix F consolidates reproducibility pointers to existing sections. The PDFs establish the added access pointer, not the repository's actual availability.

R1.justification: v2 attributes the original bandit formulation to MetaSD rather than BanditSpec, adds diffusion-drafter, deployment, and PLD references, and removes the Huang 2024 routing discussion and AdaServe citation. The claimed novelty of full-information selection remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 removes the contents page, shortens the conclusion, revises introductory attribution and captions, and adds compatibility, ethics, and reproducibility sections. These are localized narrative changes rather than a comprehensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR formatting throughout, changing typography, headers, text geometry, and figure/table sizing and placement. The overview moves into the introduction; a NormalHedge figure and Tables 13–14 are added, and Table 12 expands. Existing plots are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: REST and broader out-of-domain experiments strengthen support for the existing generality claim, while NormalHedge pseudocode and a code link improve implementation guidance. The net gain is limited: the central method and previous results are unchanged, the short Theorem 6 proof is removed, and Table 12's blanket superiority language overlooks lower Llama MultiNews throughput than EAGLE.
